newsitem.title: USA: Fire forces evacuation of NYC buildings.
newsitem.headline: Fire forces evacuation of NYC buildings.

text.p: Fire in manholes below the streets of New York City filled several buildings with thick smoke Tuesday and forced the evacuation of more than 100 children from a daycare centre, the Fire Department said.
There were no reports of injuries. The fire was reported at 10:20 a.m. EST, spewing smoke from manholes below 74th Street and York Avenue on Manhattan's Upper East Side.
Three commercial buildings were evacuated, including the daycare centre. The children were taken to a nearby church.
Members of the Fire Department were conducting tests to determine whether the smoke contained hazardous materials, officials said. The cause of the blaze was unknown.
The fire broke out near a Consolidated Edison generating plant, which also was partly evacuated, a Con Ed spokeswoman said. The fire did not appear to involve the Con Ed plant, she said.
Traffic was snarled for several blocks around the site of the fire.
